Not only is it still relevant, but count_heartbeats in is currently also broken :-)

Actually, looking at it, maybe count_heartbeats without in is currently fixed? no, on e.g. JacobiZariski it's still reporting that everything in e.g. a section takes the same number of heartbeats. So currently it's doubly broken :-(

Still seems relevant.

Test: go to random mathlib file, write #count_heartbeats at the top of it, and note that it claims that every definition and theorem takes essentially the same number of heartbeats.

Furthermore things have got slightly worse in that Damiano's workaround here no longer compiles.

Today I chose issue #23905 for discussion!

linter.countHeartbeats is broken
Created by @Kevin Buzzard (@kbuzzard) on 2025-04-10
Labels:

Is this issue still relevant? Any recent updates? Anyone making progress?

As far as I can see, (a) #count_heartbeats at the top of a file still doesn't work and furthermore (b) @Damiano Testa 's workaround #mathlib4 > Frustrating debugging problem @ 💬 from last year also no longer works (the code doesn't compile any more).

Since this hasn't progressed in a long time, and there is a reasonable alternative of using trace.profiler with trace.profiler.useHeartbeats instead of #count_heartbeats, I think we should just deprecate #count_heartbeats (and corresponding linter). (Though of course, we can keep #count_heartbeats in)

What do you think @Damiano Testa?

I don't object to this. I have a much better solution now anyway -- if I am trying to work out the changes in compile times for a file before and after a change I just ask an LLM to do a detailed analysis for me and I don't have to use any lean commands at all. LLMs are really good at this now.
